source.author: lucan
source.text: Quam prior affatur Pompeii ignava propago: O decus Haemonidum, populis quae pandere fata, Quaeque suo ventura potes divertere cursu, Te precor, ut certum liceat mihi noscere finem, Quem belli Fortuna paret.
source.text_original: Quam prior affatur Pompeii ignava propago: / O decus Haemonidum, populis quae pandere fata, / Quaeque suo ventura potes divertere cursu, / Te precor, ut certum liceat mihi noscere finem, / Quem belli Fortuna paret.
source.text_english: Then Pompey’s cowardly offspring addresses him first: O glory of the Haemonids, you who can reveal the fates to nations and avert what is to come by your own course, I beg you, let me know for certain the end that Fortune is preparing for this war.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: sin aliud Fortuna parat, miserere parentum, Mors bona, dum metus est nec adhuc dolor.
reuse.text_original: sin aliud Fortuna parat, miserere parentum, / Mors bona, dum metus est nec adhuc dolor.
reuse.text_english: But if Fortune is preparing something else, have pity on my parents, gentle Death, while there is still fear and not yet pain.
